summary: Frontend-only focused retest completed on REAL Playwright WebKit using /app/.browser-testing/bin/python. Verified frame-sequence scroll behavior (0/50/100 + reverse + idle settle) on desktop and mobile, validated delayed-routing concurrency stress with rapid direction flips and motion off/on, and spot-checked failure-retry and reduced-motion opt-in flows.
critical_code_review_comments: WebKit evidence confirms scroll state is driving canvas frames: desktop frame/targetFrame moved 0 -> 216 -> 240 and reverse back to 0; mobile moved 0 -> 229 -> 240 and reverse back to 0.
Canvas hashes changed between checkpoints and matched again at reverse+idle, indicating no frozen frame and stable settle behavior in this run.

Delayed 1200ms media routing + rapid direction flips + quick motion off/on kept observed in-flight hero-sequence requests at peak_active=2 (<=3 requirement), with drained_before_close=true and no WebKit page crash in final run.
Failure path and recovery in WebKit works: blocked source switched stage to static (no canvas), then retry restored animated canvas and frame updates.
Reduced-motion explicit activation works in WebKit: initial static state without canvas, motion toggle opt-in restored animated sequence.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Artifacts are under /app/test_reports/artifacts/iteration_6 with per-checkpoint screenshots and structured telemetry in webkit_results.json (scrollY, frame, targetFrame, stageState, canvasHash, concurrency lifecycle). Script uses REAL WebKit sync API and can be rerun directly with /app/.browser-testing/bin/python /app/tests/webkit_smoke.py.
rca of the issue: Original false-negative ('webkit_frame=0 after wheel') was caused by insufficient readiness/settle logic in the old smoke script (single short wheel + fixed 900ms wait). After adding readiness checks, track-relative scrolling, settle waits, and state telemetry, WebKit no longer reproduces the reported stuck-scroll bug in this environment.
